# pensieve

> An iOS app for notes that fade. You write something down, it expires on its
> own, and there is nothing to tidy up afterwards. "for what you carry."

pensieve is a journaling app that forgets on purpose. A note goes lighter as
the days pass and is gone in a week by default. There is no archive and no
search: once a note fades on its own it cannot be recovered, which is the
point. Notes deleted by hand sit in Trash for 30 days first.

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 17.0 or later. No iPad or Mac app.
- Price: free, no ads, no account. An optional supporter purchase unlocks
  "never", a note released that way stays until you delete it.
- Pinning is free and pauses a note's fade until you unpin it. Unpinning starts
  the note's full window again from now, rather than resuming the time the note
  had left. A single note can also be extended from its menu.
- Notes are stored on device. iCloud sync is off by default; turned on, notes
  travel through the reader's own private iCloud and never through a server
  belonging to pensieve. There is no server.
- No analytics, no tracking, no sign-up.
- Notes cannot be edited. A note stays what you wrote when you wrote it.
- Widgets for the Home Screen, Lock Screen and Control Center, plus a share
  sheet extension.

## Pages

- [Home](https://theanhgen.github.io/pensieve-site/): what the app does, how
  fading works, and the FAQ.
- [Why it forgets](https://theanhgen.github.io/pensieve-site/why.html): the
  reasoning behind a notes app with no archive.
- [Privacy policy](https://theanhgen.github.io/pensieve-site/privacy.html):
  what is collected, which is nothing.

## Status

Not yet on the App Store. The site says "coming soon" and collects an email
for launch. Any claim that it is downloadable today is wrong.
